summary: Sets out requirements for very fast setup of GMPLS Label Switched Paths, as network providers need to scale LSP creation rates, setup delay and traffic loads. It presents scaling objectives.

eli5.summary: Networks need to build their roads faster. This lists how fast and how many.

subtitle: Scaling up dynamic circuit setup for cloud and data centers

tldr.problem: Network providers need to set up large numbers of circuits quickly and frequently, but existing GMPLS protocols may not meet the performance targets needed for emerging applications like cloud computing and grid computing.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC lists specific protocol and procedure requirements to enable sub-second setup of label switched paths, including pipelined processing, support for short-lived connections, and operations across domain boundaries.
tldr.outcome: These requirements define targets for future protocol work, ensuring that circuit-switched networks can be as dynamic as packet networks while maintaining guaranteed bandwidth and low latency.

today: RFC 7709 is an Informational document that has influenced the development of faster GMPLS protocols for emerging applications. The move toward cloud computing and dynamic bandwidth allocation has made these requirements increasingly relevant. Some GMPLS extensions have been designed with these performance goals in mind, though not all implementations meet the full targets.

sections.title: The Need for Fast Circuit Setup
sections.content:
Generalized Multi-Protocol Label Switching (GMPLS) is a control protocol for networks that use circuit switching instead of packet forwarding. The RFC addresses the problem that as applications like cloud computing, grid computing, and data visualization emerge, networks need to set up circuits much faster than existing GMPLS implementations support.

Unlike static circuits that carry traffic for hours or days, emerging applications need to request circuits on demand, sometimes for only a few seconds. The control protocols that set up these circuits must not be the bottleneck. Current GMPLS procedures focus on robustness and error recovery but do not prioritize speed, which is now a requirement.
sections.eli5: Computers in data centers now want to request temporary network connections very quickly, maybe for just a few seconds. The control systems need to be able to set those up almost instantly so the control system is not the slow part.

sections.title: Emerging Applications and Traffic Patterns
sections.content:
The document describes the target environment as arising from programs like the DARPA CORONET (Core Optical Networks) program, which addresses highly dynamic, multi-terabit networks serving cloud, grid, and visualization applications. The expected traffic pattern includes many bandwidth-on-demand requests per second, with individual connections lasting as little as one second.

Applications span cloud services that need to move data quickly between locations, grid computing jobs that shift work between sites, and large data transfers between data centers. The aggregate traffic demand is five to twenty times higher than current carrier traffic levels. Meeting these demands with dynamic circuits instead of static packet services can provide guaranteed bandwidth and lower latency than packet networks.
sections.eli5: Lots of new applications need to move data around very quickly. Cloud services, universities doing research, and video companies all need the ability to set up fast connections between their servers whenever they need them.

sections.title: Key Performance Requirements
sections.content:
The RFC identifies two core requirements. First, connection request rates should range from a few requests per second for high-bandwidth wavelengths (40 Gb/s, 100 Gb/s) to around 100 requests per second for sub-wavelength circuits. Second, connection setup delay should be around 100 milliseconds across a national or regional network, assuming a network with up to 100 nodes and distances up to 3000 km.

To achieve 100 ms setup time with up to 15 hops, the maximum processing delay per hop must be around 700 microseconds, with optimal path selection and resource allocation requiring up to 5 milliseconds at the source or destination. Pipelined cross-connection must be enabled so that data path availability is bounded by the worst-case single-node processing time, not by the total time across all nodes.
sections.eli5: The goal is to set up a connection from coast to coast in about one-tenth of a second, and to be able to start hundreds of new connections every second without the control system slowing things down.

sections.title: Protocol and Procedure Requirements
sections.content:
The RFC lists eight requirements for GMPLS protocol design. The protocol must scale linearly with the number of hops (R1), enable pipelined processing (R2), avoid off-path control transactions that could introduce delay (R3), support very short holding times of one second or less (R4), and handle request rates of tens per second (R5). Requirements also cover failure recovery faster than standard crank-back procedures (R6), multi-domain networks (R7), and compatibility with existing GMPLS requirements (R8).

The requirements target cases where expedited setup is essential, and they acknowledge that some trade-offs with robustness may be necessary in cases where speed is more important than recovery from all possible setup errors.
sections.eli5: The control system should not add much delay regardless of how many routers are involved, should not need to wait for separate permission from other devices, and should be able to handle hundreds of connection requests without getting slower.

sections.title: Security and Encryption Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC notes that very fast setup and high churn rates should not adversely affect existing GMPLS security mechanisms. However, if encryption with key exchange is needed on the circuits, the extra round-trip time for key exchange will impact setup speed and churn rates. The document suggests that key exchange can be amortized across multiple exchanges between the same peers, potentially using zero-round-trip-time (zero-RTT) mode to avoid blocking on key establishment.

The point is that speed requirements must be considered early if encryption is to be added later, rather than being retrofitted and causing unexpected delays.
sections.eli5: If the network needs to encrypt the data passing through the circuits, the encryption setup time will slow down the overall connection setup time. This needs to be planned for ahead of time.
